slides.5.title: 🎓 Key Takeaways
slides.5.points.0: ✓ Alto Adige: Speck smoked ham + Pinot Grigio (regional pairing); Goulash braised beef + Lagrein (South Tyrol native pairing)
slides.5.points.1: ✓ Friuli: San Daniele ham + Friulano; Frico cheese-potato cake + high-acid Ribolla Gialla; orange wine pairing is Friuli's signature
slides.5.points.2: ✓ Liguria: Trenette al Pesto must pair with Vermentino/Pigato — herbs meet herbs
slides.5.points.3: ✓ Emilia-Romagna: Lambrusco semi-sparkling red is the all-purpose fat-cutter for the charcuterie trio (ham, sausage, aged cheese)
slides.5.points.4: ✓ Parmigiano's saltiness offsets the negative effect of umami, making high-acid red wine pairing possible (salt is wine's best friend)
slides.5.points.5: ✓ Franciacorta + Cotoletta alla Milanese: sparkling wine cuts fried-food fat — northern Italy's premium pairing formula
slides.5.points.6: ✓ Amarone suits rich braised and air-dried meats; Soave suits seafood and white meats — both Veneto, but weight must still match the dish
slides.5.points.7: ✓ Northern Italy core logic: high-mountain whites cut richness; sparkling wine universally cleanses; always seek local wine for local food
slides.6.title: 🧠 Northern Italy Pairing Knowledge Check
quiz.0.question: Which pairing best follows the regional principle for South Tyrol Speck smoked ham?
quiz.0.explanation: 'What grows together, goes together' — Speck is Alto Adige's traditional cured meat, and the same-region Pinot Grigio's fresh fruitiness cuts through the smoky fat. This is the most regionally authentic pairing.
quiz.1.question: Why is Lambrusco the best pairing for Emilia-Romagna charcuterie (ham, sausage)?
quiz.1.options.0: Because Lambrusco has high alcohol, which sanitises
quiz.1.options.1: Because Lambrusco's semi-sparkling bubbles cut through pork fat, while its off-dry fruit balances the salty richness
quiz.1.options.2: Because Lambrusco has extremely high tannins that bind to proteins
quiz.1.options.3: Because Lambrusco is the world's most expensive wine
quiz.1.explanation: Lambrusco's value lies in its bubbles and fruit: carbonation mechanically cuts pork fat (like sparkling water), while the off-dry fruitiness balances the salty richness of Prosciutto and Mortadella. A thousand years of co-evolution created this perfect match.
quiz.2.question: What is the best pairing for Cotoletta alla Milanese (Milanese veal cutlet)?
quiz.2.explanation: Fried foods need high-acid sparkling wine to cut the oil. Franciacorta Brut's fine bubbles and high acidity perfectly refresh the palate — this is Milan's most traditional pairing. Barolo/Amarone are too full-bodied and would overpower the cutlet; Moscato's sweetness is inappropriate.
quiz.3.question: Which wine is most suitable for Ligurian Trenette al Pesto (basil pesto pasta)?
quiz.3.explanation: Vermentino's natural herbal notes perfectly resonate with pesto's basil, pine nuts and garlic — and as Liguria's native variety, it is the most regionally authentic choice. Avoid full-bodied reds, which would overpower pesto's delicate aromatics.
